title: Quantum Tsallis Entropy Estimation: Near-Optimal Bounds and High-Precision Improvements
authors: Chengshen Gao, Zongxing Xiong, Lvzhou Li
abstract: Estimating statistical properties of probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistics and theoretical computer science. We develop quantum algorithms for estimating the $q$-Tsallis entropy $\mathrm{H}_q^{\mathrm{Tsa}}(P) =\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^q-1}{1-q}$ when $0<q<1$, given purified quantum query access to a distribution $P$ on $[n]$. When $0<q\leq \frac{1}{2}$, we provide a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\rbra{\left(\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{1}{2q}}}$, which is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. When $\frac{1}{2}<q<1$, we introduce a two-stage simultaneous probability estimation procedure, yielding a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{n^{\frac12+\frac{1}{2q}}}{\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2q}}}+\frac{n^{1-q}}{\varepsilon}\right)$, which improves the result given by Chen et al. (ICALP 2026) when $\varepsilon=O\rbra{n^{1-2q}}$.
summary: This paper presents quantum algorithms to estimate the $q$-Tsallis entropy for a given probability distribution. By developing distinct, optimized procedures for $q \le 1/2$ and $q > 1/2$, the authors achieve query complexities that approach known lower bounds, marking significant theoretical improvements in quantum information processing.
main_problem: The paper develops quantum algorithms to estimate the $q$-Tsallis entropy, $H_q(P)$, for a probability distribution $P$ given purified quantum query access.
main_result: It achieves near-optimal query complexities for estimating $H_q(P)$ in two distinct regimes: $\widetilde{O}((n/\epsilon)^{1/2q})$ for $0 < q \le 1/2$, and an improved bound for $1/2 < q < 1$.
method: The methods involve adapting a multilevel framework using quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) for $q \le 1/2$, and employing a two-stage simultaneous probability estimation procedure combined with quantum mean estimation for $q > 1/2$.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed in the abstract model of purified quantum query access to a classical probability distribution $P$ on $n$ outcomes. The focus is on the mathematical estimation of the entropy functional.
key_observables: The $q$-Tsallis entropy, $H_q(P)$, and related power sums, $F_q(P) = \sum p_i q^i$.
important_parameters: The order of the entropy, $q$ ($0 < q < 1$), the number of outcomes $n$, and the desired accuracy $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The algorithms assume purified quantum query access via a unitary oracle $U_P$. The analysis relies on specific quantum subroutines like Amplitude Estimation and Mean Estimation.
figures_summary: The notes refer to a comparison table (Table 1) summarizing the derived upper bounds against existing results and lower bounds for different regimes of $q$.
paper_structure: The paper is structured by analyzing the problem in two regimes: $0 < q \le 1/2$ (using a multilevel framework and QSVT) and $1/2 < q < 1$ (using a two-stage estimation procedure). It builds upon previous work by improving complexity bounds.
why_interesting: This work directly advances the field of quantum algorithms for statistical estimation, providing concrete, near-optimal complexity results for a non-standard entropy measure (Tsallis entropy) in the quantum query model.
